The last drops of the precipitate washed water is treated with AgN03 solution and BaC12 solution in separate test tubes. Formation of a white ppt indicates the presence of chloride and carbonate ions respectively.
Wash the ppt till it is free from chloride and carbonate ions.
Dry the ppt over the Bunsen burner or in air oven.

RESULT
The insoluble components (CaC03 and sand) were separated from their mixture by dissolving the mixture in a suitable solvent (dil. HCl) followed by filtration, precipitation, washing and drying.
PRECAUTIONS
All the glasswares should be handled with care.
Instead of dil. HCl, dil. H2S04 should not be used since insoluble CaS04 will be formed.
There should not be any loss of the amount of sand and the ppt of CaC03.
The precipitation of CaC03 should be complete.

THEORY

The solid or liquid substances which convert easily into vapour form by the little supply of heat or on exposure to atmosphere are called volatile substances. For example: camphor, ammonium chloride, iodine, petrol etc.

The mixture of sand, camphor and common salt is separated by sublimation process followed by filtration. The volatile component of the mixture (here, camphor) is separated from the non-volatile one by sublimation processe Sublimation can be defined as the process Of converting the solid directly into the vapour and cooling back the vapour directly into the solid state. Thus obtained solid is called sublimate.
Carnphor is obtained as a sublimate from the given mixture.

The rest of the components of the mixture (i.e. sand and common salt) are separated by dissolution of the mixture in water followed by filtration. Sand is obtained as residue whereas solution of common salt is obtained in solid form by evaporating its solutione Filtration is defined as the method of separating the insoluble component and solution of the soluble component of the mixture by means of a porous medium like filter paper, glass wool etc.
